correctness.rationale: The monomial norm is exactly kappa+M_n and is equivalent to H2 for kappa>0. The moments M_n decrease from one to zero and reciprocal coefficients increase from 1/(1+kappa) to 1/kappa. The telescoping increment identity proves the sharp modulus inequality for every scalar product t in the claimed disk. Center mass gives exact equality and the sharp product-coordinate zero; locally uniform convergence of smooth beta radial weights to that center-mass kernel and Rouche yield simple real zeros for every kappa<1. The separate alpha=3 finite witness has rigorous rational-tail bounds obtained by running embedded checker.py. The refined displacement follows from the first-order expansion determined by M_1=1/(alpha+2), M_n<=M_2=O(alpha^-2) for n>=2, and the nonzero rational-limit derivative.

value.rationale: This sharp uniform criterion and radius describe robustness of Lu Qi-Keng nonvanishing under an added boundary Hardy energy for all radial probability measures, independent of density smoothness. A quantitative extremal inequality and smooth below-threshold counterexamples separate universally safe mass from vulnerable mass. Each constituent weighted Bergman or Hardy kernel can be zero-free while their summed norm has a zero; this is a meaningful structural distinction, not a one-off numeric fact. The explicit exterior displacement quantifies approach to the optimal radius.
